evals.prompt: sarah left 4 comments on PR #287, mostly about the error handling in the webhook handler. can you go through them, fix what makes sense, and reply to each one? skip the rebase, I already did that
evals.expected_output: Fetches comments on PR #287, triages by confidence, applies fixes for accepted comments, skips rebase phase, commits with conventional format, replies to reviewers, resolves threads, and pushes
expectations: triggers pr-fix skill and fetches review comments for PR #287
skips Phase 5 (rebase) because --skip-rebase intent is expressed
applies code fixes to the webhook handler error handling based on accepted feedback
commits changes using conventional commit format (e.g., 'fix: address PR review feedback')
posts reply comments to each addressed comment and resolves their threads via GraphQL

evals.expected_output: Runs the full 10-phase remediation workflow in auto mode, accepting fixes scoring 90+ and skipping those below, then rebases, commits, replies, resolves threads, and pushes
expectations: operates in non-interactive auto mode without prompting the user
uses 90 as the confidence threshold instead of the default 95
auto-accepts fixes scoring >= 90 and skips those below with a log entry
executes the full 10-phase workflow: fetch, analyze, rebase, apply, test, commit, push, reply, resolve, report
pushes with --force-with-lease after rebase rewrites history

evals.expected_output: Analyzes and scores all comments, shows the remediation plan with proposed fixes and confidence breakdowns, but does not apply any changes, commit, or push
expectations: fetches and categorizes all review comments with priority levels (P0-P3, Info)
computes confidence scores for each comment using Technical Accuracy (35%), Code Evidence (30%), Clear Remediation (20%), Scope Impact (15%)
displays the categorized comment list with proposed fixes and confidence scores
does NOT apply any code changes, create commits, or push to remote
labels the summary report as 'DRY RUN — no changes were made'

evals.prompt: fix all the review comments on my PR end to end — the full pipeline, rebase, commit, push, everything
evals.expected_output: Executes the complete 10-phase workflow: fetch comments, triage by confidence, apply fixes, rebase onto base branch, commit, reply to reviewers, resolve threads, and push
expectations: executes phases in order: init, fetch, triage, remediate, rebase, commit, reply, resolve, push, summary
rebase onto base branch happens BEFORE applying commits
commits use conventional commit format with fix:/refactor:/style: prefix
thread resolution via GraphQL happens AFTER pushing changes
generates a completion report showing comments processed, fixes applied/skipped/rejected, threads resolved

evals.expected_output: Fixes comments on PR #123, skips the rebase phase, and pushes with --force-with-lease
expectations: operates on PR #123 specifically, not the current branch PR
skips Phase 5 (rebase) entirely due to --skip-rebase flag
pushes with git push --force-with-lease (NOT bare --force) due to --force flag
stages only the files modified during remediation — never uses git add -A or git add .
checks out the correct branch for PR #123 if not already on it

evals.prompt: the PR has 2 blocking comments from jake about a null pointer bug and a race condition. fix those ASAP, skip the style nits from other reviewers
evals.expected_output: Prioritizes P0 blocking comments, applies fixes for the null pointer and race condition issues, skips lower-priority suggestions, commits and pushes
expectations: categorizes blocking comments as P0 priority and processes them first
applies fixes for the null pointer bug and race condition as high-priority remediations
skips or deprioritizes P2 style/nit suggestions per user intent
reads the referenced source files before applying fixes to verify code context
replies to fixed comments with 'Fixed in <commit-sha-short>' template

evals.prompt: there are like 8 comments on PR #55 from the review. some are legit bugs, some are just opinions. fix the real issues, explain why I'm not changing the opinionated ones, and push it all up
evals.expected_output: Triages all 8 comments by confidence, fixes high-confidence bug reports, posts rejection explanations for opinion-based comments, resolves fixed threads, and pushes
expectations: uses confidence scoring to distinguish legitimate bugs (high Technical Accuracy) from opinion-based comments (lower scores)
applies code fixes only for comments that pass the confidence threshold
posts rejection replies with technical reasoning for comments not applied
resolves threads only for comments that were actually fixed — leaves rejected threads open
generates the final summary report with disposition counts per priority category

evals.expected_output: Runs full remediation in auto mode with default 95% confidence threshold, auto-fixing high-confidence items and logging skipped ones
expectations: uses the default confidence threshold of 95% in auto mode
auto-accepts fixes scoring >= 95 without prompting the user
skips all fixes below 95% with a log entry — does not prompt
verifies each fix after applying (syntax check, linter if available) and reverts if broken
never adds AI attribution lines to commits — no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with signatures

evals.prompt: PR #200 got 12 comments across 6 files. address everything, but I want to see a confidence breakdown before you start fixing anything. also don't rebase, and use force push when done
evals.expected_output: Shows confidence breakdown for all 12 comments first, then applies accepted fixes interactively, skips rebase, commits, and force-pushes with --force-with-lease
expectations: presents confidence breakdown with per-comment scores before applying any fixes
operates in interactive mode — prompts for sub-threshold comments with the breakdown visible
skips rebase phase as requested
pushes with git push --force-with-lease origin <branch> — NOT bare --force
fetches both inline code review comments and top-level PR conversation comments

evals.prompt: mike asked 3 questions in the PR review and also left a suggestion about renaming the config struct. answer his questions and apply the rename if it makes sense
evals.expected_output: Answers the 3 questions with direct responses via reply comments, evaluates the rename suggestion by confidence, applies if accepted, commits and pushes
expectations: categorizes the 3 questions as P3 (Question) and the rename as P2 (Suggestion)
posts direct answer replies to each question using the Question Response template
evaluates the rename suggestion with confidence scoring before applying
if rename is accepted, applies the change minimally without refactoring surrounding code
commits with appropriate conventional commit type (fix: or refactor: depending on changes)
